title: Microsoft Purview: network data security with Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access)
summary: The briefing passes: the network protection controls, licensing and administrator-configured default are supported by Microsoft's current documentation. The earlier fetch failures were not missing pages; only minor path abbreviations, a missing source citation and checklist/table coverage need correction.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview wizard path reaches Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers.
claims.quote: Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list.
claims.fix: Use the full path: Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers. The omitted cloud-app and user-scope selections are permissible abbreviations.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Network") creates a DLP policy with network enforcement.
claims.quote: The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. This parameter uses the following syntax: -EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>"). Valid values are: ... Network

claims.claim: The printed Entra Content policies creation path reaches Action > Scan with Purview.
claims.quote: On the Basics tab: ... On the Rules tab: ... Select the appropriate option for the Action menu: ... To use data policies configured in Microsoft Purview, select Scan with Purview.
claims.fix: Use Global Secure Access > Secure > Content policies > + Create Policy > Basics > Rules > Add rule > Action > Scan with Purview. Add rule is explicitly documented in the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/global-secure-access/tutorial-internet-access-content-policies.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row; Open questions
claims.claim: An API for configuring the Entra content-policy rule's Scan with Purview action is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Global Secure Access content policies Scan with Purview API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph/api networkaccess contentFilteringPolicy contentPolicy ScanWithPurview create; read content-filtering guide, Graph Internet Access tutorial and filteringPolicy create/resource references.

claims.claim: The printed Entra Conditional Access creation path reaches Use Global Secure Access Security Profile.
claims.quote: Set the Target resources to All internet resources with Global Secure Access. ... Under Session, select Use Global Secure Access Security Profile and select the security profile you created.
claims.fix: Use Identity > Protection > Conditional Access > + Create new policy > Target resources > All internet resources with Global Secure Access > Session > Use Global Secure Access Security Profile. The omitted resource-scope selection is a permissible abbreviation, not a wrong route.

claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies ... In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a conditionalAccessPolicy object.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The Entra integration inspects text, prompts and files from managed endpoints using Purview network data security.
claims.quote: These controls apply to content shared from managed endpoints ... It inspects files and text for sensitive information and helps prevent data loss by blocking its sharing based on your Purview DLP policies.

claims.claim: The integration covers traffic through browsers, applications, add-ins and APIs.
claims.quote: These controls apply to content shared from managed endpoints through browsers, applications, add-ins, APIs, and more.

claims.claim: Generative AI interactions are supported network data security targets.
claims.quote: Interactions with generative AI through browsers, apps, and add-ins, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude.

claims.claim: Network data security can protect files uploaded to unsanctioned cloud storage.
claims.quote: Files uploaded to unsanctioned cloud storage providers, including Dropbox, Box, and Google Drive.

claims.claim: Cloud webmail is a supported network data security destination.
claims.quote: Emails and file attachments shared with cloud email providers, such as Gmail.

claims.claim: Social media posts are supported network data security interactions.
claims.quote: Social media posts on common services like Facebook and X.

claims.claim: The roadmap description includes detecting risky user activity through Insider Risk Management.
claims.quote: detect risky user activity through Insider Risk Management

claims.claim: The roadmap describes managing alerts and incidents through Purview and Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: while managing alerts and incidents through Purview and Microsoft Defender.

claims.quote: Actions - Network data security supports Audit only and Block actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Blocking HTML or JSON text types can unintentionally block ordinary web and API traffic.
claims.quote: Web requests and responses commonly use HTML or JSON payloads, so blocking these text types can unintentionally block normal web and API traffic, including GET, POST, and PUT operations.

claims.claim: Exceeding API rate limits blocks network content-filtering traffic fail-closed.

claims.quote: Configure the Session type condition to scope the rule by traffic origin. Select Agent to match traffic classified as AI agent traffic.

claims.claim: TLS inspection is required for the content-policy deployment.
claims.quote: Content policies require Transport Layer Security (TLS) inspection to be enabled. Security service edge (SSE) can't detect file types within encrypted uploads unless the traffic is decrypted.
